title: Flaky Cong You Bing Chinese Scallion Pancakes
summary: A hot-water dough is brushed with sesame-oil paste and spring onions, rolled up and coiled into spirals, flattened and pan-fried covered then uncovered until crisp and deep golden.
equipment: 25 cm cast-iron or heavy frying pan with lid

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus 1 tbsp and extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dip
steps.text: Whisk the soy, spring onion, water, vinegar, honey, sesame oil and chilli.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix flour with boiling water, knead 4 minutes and rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Laminate
steps.text: Roll each half thin, brush with the oil paste, add salt and spring onion, roll up and coil.

steps.title: Roll out
steps.text: Flatten each coil to 23 cm and cut a small slit in the centre.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Cook covered on each side, then uncovered until deep golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut into wedges and serve with the dip.

tips: Boiling water makes a soft dough that rolls thin without springing back.
The coil is what creates the flaky layers; do not skip it.
Shake the pan while frying so the pancake puffs evenly.
storage: Freeze shaped, uncooked pancakes between baking paper for up to 1 month and fry from thawed. Cooked pancakes are best eaten at once. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
